answer: Riddikulus turns the boggart into a shape the caster finds funny. The caster must hold a clear comic image in mind while casting, because the word alone will not force the change.

Dementors drain hope and happiness, and a group of them is harder to hold off than one. Simply enduring them does not remove that pressure, so defence needs a positive force the dementor cannot feed on, which is why the Patronus is taught separately.

Thestrals are said to bring misfortune, and the Ministry labels them dangerous. In practice only people who have seen death can see them, and they are not normally dangerous, though they may bite when annoyed.

Ordinary werewolves are people who face prejudice and legal barriers, while Greyback is an exceptional predator who attacks without the full moon. Treating Greyback as the model for every werewolf turns fear into prejudice and makes unjust laws easier to accept.

A Secrecy Sensor detects concealment and Dark magic, but it can be set off by ordinary dishonesty and needs someone to read the signal. The Fidelius Charm instead hides a secret inside a living Secret-Keeper, and the secret cannot be found unless that person chooses to reveal it.

Protego deflects minor jinxes so that they rebound on the attacker. It cannot stop Avada Kedavra, because there is no countercurse or block for the Killing Curse, so the caster has to know what the shield can and cannot stop.

The Fidelius Charm hides a secret inside a Secret-Keeper, and the secret stays hidden unless that person chooses to reveal it. The charm's weakness is human trust rather than spell strength, because the Secret-Keeper can always decide to speak.

The Disarming Charm removes an opponent's wand and can knock them off balance, which makes it a strong opening move. Its limit is predictability, because opponents who expect it can prepare a different response, so a duellist must vary the attack.

answer: Riddikulus destroys the boggart by forcing it back into the wardrobe. The caster only needs to say the word loudly.
A dementor feeds on hope and happiness, so it is not enough to endure it; defence needs a positive force that the creature cannot drain. That is why the separate discipline exists.

Thestrals are widely said to bring misfortune, and the Ministry classifies them as dangerous, which shapes how people react to them. The truth is that only a person who has witnessed death can see a thestral at all, so the creature's reputation is tied to that experience rather than to ordinary aggression. They are not normally dangerous, although they may bite if they are really annoyed. Their bad name comes from the death connection, not from a habit of attacking people, and a calm handler can work with them.
Greyback is an exception and most werewolves are ordinary people, so fear of him should not condemn them all. At the same time, all werewolves are dangerous and should be treated as predators.
A Secrecy Sensor is useful in a classroom because it can be noisy. Fidelius is a very old spell and old spells are usually powerful.
Fidelius makes a house invisible to everyone except the caster. The charm can be broken by a strong enough countercurse.

The Disarming Charm is useful because it can take an opponent's wand out of the fight and may also knock them off balance, giving the caster an opening. It is a reliable basic spell and works well as a first move in a duel. The limit is that it becomes predictable: once opponents know the caster favours it, they can watch for it and prepare a different response. A duellist therefore has to vary the attack and not rely on the same spell every time. The charm is not weak, but it is not a complete strategy on its own.
